title: The Merchant of Teeth
text: A smiling trader leans on a cart of fine things, silver and silk and blades, a necklace of human teeth clicking at his throat. He wants nothing you carry, he says, nothing at all. He wants a little of you. Just a little.

options.label: The Leader trades a little of themselves, for something very fine.

outcomes.text: He takes something you will not miss for years, and hands over something fine. The Leader's step is a little slower after.

options.label: The cleverest haggles him down, and tries to keep their teeth.

outcomes.text: He is delighted to be bested, and pays for the lesson.
He is delighted, and takes a tooth for his trouble, root and all, and adds it to his necklace.

options.label: Refuse him politely, and keep every part of yourselves.

outcomes.text: It shrugs and trundles off, still smiling. In the morning the Leader has a loose tooth that was not loose before.

options.label: The Pugilist offers him some teeth. Not their own.

outcomes.text: He is delighted, with the teeth and the knuckles both, and pays in iron rings that fit over them.
He takes the teeth, and then some of the Pugilist's, for his trouble.
